subject: komodo dragon
title: What If a Komodo Dragon Bit You?

scenes.text: What if a Komodo dragon bit you? Its bite is weak, and that's the bad news.
Its jaws squeeze with about a sixth of a crocodile's force. It grips, then rips back with serrated teeth.
Two long venom glands run down its jaw, packed with toxins that stop your blood from clotting.
Your blood pressure crashes toward shock. Just 4 milligrams of venom can do that to a 40 kilogram deer.
For decades, people blamed deadly bacteria in its mouth. No one ever documented a victim dying that way.
The real weapon was venom all along, and one full gland holds at least eight times that deer dose.

description:
What if a Komodo dragon bit you? A 2009 study (Fry et al., PNAS) found its bite force is far weaker than a crocodile's of similar size; it bites lightly and tears with serrated teeth.
Two venom glands in the lower jaw deliver toxins that stop blood clotting and cause shock from collapsing blood pressure: about 4 mg could send a 40 kg deer into shock, and a full gland holds at least eight times that. The old idea that mouth bacteria kill its prey was never backed by a documented case.
